Whose State
Is It, Anyway?

Which state is the server's, which is yours — and where each piece belongs.

Lesson 1 · Two kinds of state

Server state is a copy you don't own

Client stateServer state
Source of truthThis browser tabA database on the other side of the network
Who can change itOnly your codeOther users, other tabs, a cron job — without telling you
Can it go stale?Never — it is the truthThe moment it arrives
Reading itSynchronousAsync: loading, error, retry, refetch
In RasmiFilters drawer open, apply-form draftListings, saved jobs, application statuses
If someone else can change it without telling you, it's server state — and what your app holds is a cache of it. Caches need expiry, refetching and invalidation. useState has none of those.

Lesson 1 · Sorting Rasmi's state

Every piece of state gets exactly one home

The trap is Saved jobs. The user decides it, so it feels like client state — but the server keeps it. The click isn't the state; it's a request to change the server's state.

Lesson 2 · The cache

One key, one entry, one lifecycle

export const jobsQuery = (filters: JobFilters) =>
  queryOptions({
    queryKey: ['jobs', 'list', filters],                     // the entry's address
    queryFn: ({ signal }) => api.jobs(filters, { signal }),
    staleTime: 30_000,                                       // fresh for 30 s: no refetch
  });

useQuery(jobsQuery({ q: 'react', remote: true, page: 1 }));
staleTime decides when data is refetched; gcTime decides when it is deleted. Stale data still renders instantly — the refetch runs behind it.

Lesson 2 · What invalidation really means

Invalidate means “mark stale”, not “delete”

Applying to a job

const apply = useMutation({
  mutationFn: api.apply,
  onSuccess: (_res, { jobId }) =>
    Promise.all([
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({
        queryKey: ['applications'],
      }),
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({
        queryKey: ['jobs', 'detail', jobId],
      }),
    ]),
});

Four ways to touch the cache

CallWhat happens
invalidateQueriesMarks matches stale. Active ones refetch now, the rest on next use. Old data stays on screen.
setQueryDataYou write the entry. No request.
removeQueriesDeletes it. The next reader starts from loading.
refetchQueriesFetches now, stale or not.
Keys match by prefix: ['jobs'] hits every list and every detail. Shape your keys the way your data changes.

Lesson 2 · Optimistic updates

Save the job now — and keep a way back

const save = useMutation({
  mutationFn: (jobId: string) => api.saveJob(jobId),
  onMutate: async (jobId) => {
    await queryClient.cancelQueries({ queryKey: ['saved'] });                      // 1 · stop refetches in flight
    const previous = queryClient.getQueryData<string[]>(['saved']);                // 2 · snapshot
    queryClient.setQueryData<string[]>(['saved'], (old = []) => [...old, jobId]);  // 3 · write the guess
    return { previous };                                                           // 4 · hand the snapshot on
  },
  onError: (_err, _jobId, snapshot) => {
    queryClient.setQueryData(['saved'], snapshot?.previous);                       // the rollback
  },
  onSettled: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['saved'] }),         // then the server's answer wins
});
Most hand-written optimistic updates skip two lines: the onError restore, and the cancelQueries that stops a refetch already in flight from landing on top of your guess. Without them the star lies.
MODULE 08 · VIDEO 2
09 / 22
Lesson 2 · The race it fixes

A late answer lands in its own key — not on screen

const { q } = Route.useSearch();
const jobs = useQuery({
  queryKey: ['jobs', 'list', { q }],
  queryFn: ({ signal }) => api.jobs({ q }, { signal }),  // aborted once nobody observes the old key
  placeholderData: keepPreviousData,                     // keep the old list on screen while the new one loads
});
In a bare useEffect the slow re answer overwrites react. Here the screen reads by key, not arrival order — the race is designed out.

Lesson 3 · Search params as state

If it lives in useState, nobody can share it

Belongs in the URL

Search text, filters, sort, page, the open job's id, the selected tab — anything a refresh, a shared link or the back button should bring back.

Doesn't

Hover and focus, the search box before its debounce, form drafts, anything secret — a token in a URL ends up in logs and history.

Move the filters into the URL and you get three features for free: refresh keeps them, a link shares them, and Back undoes the last one.

Lesson 3 · Type-safe routes and loaders

Validate the URL once, at the route

const jobSearch = z.object({
  q: z.string().catch(''),
  remote: z.boolean().catch(false),
  page: z.number().int().min(1).catch(1),
});

export const Route = createFileRoute('/jobs')({
  validateSearch: jobSearch,                                               // ?page=abc becomes page 1, never a crash
  loaderDeps: ({ search: { q, remote, page } }) => ({ q, remote, page }),
  loader: ({ context: { queryClient }, deps }) =>
    queryClient.ensureQueryData(jobsQuery(deps)),                          // the fetch starts before render
  component: JobsPage,
});
.catch() turns a hand-edited URL into a valid default instead of an error page. loaderDeps names what the loader reads, so changing anything else in the URL doesn't refetch.

Lesson 3 · Loaders and typed links

Fetch on navigation, not on render

function JobsPage() {
  const search = Route.useSearch();                      // { q: string; remote: boolean; page: number }
  const { data } = useSuspenseQuery(jobsQuery(search));  // the loader already filled this entry
  return <Link from={Route.fullPath} search={(prev) => ({ ...prev, page: prev.page + 1 })}>Next</Link>;
}

<Link to="/jobs/$jobId" params={{ jobId: job.id }} />    // ok
<Link to="/job/$jobId" params={{ jobId: job.id }} />     // ✗ type error: no such route

Lesson 4 · Normalization

One job, three copies, two of them wrong

const jobsAdapter = createEntityAdapter<Job>();        // { ids: [], entities: {} }
const jobsSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'jobs',
  initialState: jobsAdapter.getInitialState(),
  reducers: { jobsReceived: jobsAdapter.upsertMany },  // one record per id, however many lists show it
});
With a server cache you rarely normalize — you invalidate the keys and refetch. Normalize when the client edits one record from many screens: offline drafts, editors, collaborative boards.

Lesson 4 · Zustand and Redux Toolkit

One tray, two stores

Zustand

A hook with a selector. No provider, no action types.

export const useCompare = create<{
  ids: string[];
  toggle: (id: string) => void;
}>()((set) => ({
  ids: [],
  toggle: (id) => set((s) => ({
    ids: s.ids.includes(id)
      ? s.ids.filter((x) => x !== id)
      : [...s.ids, id],
  })),
}));
// in any component:
const ids = useCompare((s) => s.ids);

Redux Toolkit

A store, a provider, actions. More ceremony, more structure.

const compare = createSlice({
  name: 'compare',
  initialState: { ids: [] as string[] },
  reducers: {
    toggle(state, a: PayloadAction<string>) {
      const i = state.ids.indexOf(a.payload);
      if (i === -1) state.ids.push(a.payload);
      else state.ids.splice(i, 1);
    },
  },
});
useAppSelector((s) => s.compare.ids);
dispatch(compare.actions.toggle(job.id));
Neither should ever hold a job listing. Stores are for state the server has never heard of.

Lesson 4 · Choosing, and refusing

Every tool here is the wrong choice somewhere

ToolRight forWrong when
useState · useReducerOne component and its childrenDistant branches need it — prop drilling starts
ContextValues that rarely change: theme, locale, userIt changes often — every consumer re-renders
ZustandSmall client state shared across the treeYou copy server data in and rebuild a cache by hand
Redux ToolkitBig client-side domains, many contributorsA small app — all ceremony, nothing to organize
TanStack QueryAnything the server ownsPurely local UI state — it's a cache, not a store
URL search paramsFilters, sort, page, the open job's idSecrets, large blobs, every keystroke
Server data copied into Zustand or Redux is the classic red flag: loading flags, staleness and refetching, rebuilt by hand — and worse.

Lesson 5 · Definition of done

Seven checks before you call it done

CheckProve it
1 · No fetching in effectsEvery read is a useQuery, useSuspenseQuery or a route loader
2 · Filters live in the URLReload, or paste the link in a private window: same results. ?page=abc lands on page 1
3 · No stale search resultsThrottle the network and type fast: the list always matches the box
4 · Save is optimistic, with rollbackMake the save endpoint fail: the star flips, then flips back with an error
5 · Apply refreshes its dependants“My applications” and the job's Applied badge update with no reload
6 · Statuses stay freshrefetchInterval on applications: change a status on the server, the badge updates within 30 s — no click
7 · The store holds no server dataZustand contains the compare tray's ids — nothing else
In the PR description, name the home of every piece of state with one sentence on why. That paragraph is your interview answer.

Module 08 · done

Every piece of state has an owner and a home

What you can now do

  • Tell server state from client statethe server owns it; what you hold is a cache
  • Run a cache instead of fetching in effectskeys, staleTime vs gcTime, invalidation, optimistic updates that roll back
  • Close race conditions for goodcleanup flags, AbortController, or keys that decide
  • Keep shareable state in a typed URLvalidateSearch, loaders, typed links
  • Pick a store — or refuse oneZustand, Redux Toolkit, Context, or the cache you already have
